<thought>By analyzing the measured resistances, I discovered that every node lies on a single linear series path from A to B. The distance (resistance) from A to each node matches the sum of resistances of consecutive segments, and the sum of the distance from A to a node plus the distance from that node to B always equals the total A‑B resistance (125 Ω). Therefore the circuit is a simple series chain connecting the nodes in the order:
A – X1 – N_b1 – X2 – N_c1 – N_c2 – N_c3 – X3 – N_d1 – N_d2 – N_d3 – B.

The resistor values are the differences between successive node positions (resistances from A):
A‑X1 = 6.667 Ω,
X1‑N_b1 = 5 Ω,
N_b1‑X2 = 13.333 Ω,
X2‑N_c1 = 5 Ω,
N_c1‑N_c2 = 10 Ω,
N_c2‑N_c3 = 15 Ω,
N_c3‑X3 = 20 Ω,
X3‑N_d1 = 5 Ω,
N_d1‑N_d2 = 10 Ω,
N_d2‑N_d3 = 15 Ω,
N_d3‑B = 20 Ω.

These values reproduce all given measurements. The required JSON describing the topology is therefore:</thought>
<final_answer>{
  "resistors": {
    "R1": 6.667,
    "R2": 5,
    "R3": 13.333,
    "R4": 5,
    "R5": 10,
    "R6": 15,
    "R7": 20,
    "R8": 5,
    "R9": 10,
    "R10": 15,
    "R11": 20
  },
  "connections": [
    ["A", "X1", "R1"],
    ["X1", "N_b1", "R2"],
    ["N_b1", "X2", "R3"],
    ["X2", "N_c1", "R4"],
    ["N_c1", "N_c2", "R5"],
    ["N_c2", "N_c3", "R6"],
    ["N_c3", "X3", "R7"],
    ["X3", "N_d1", "R8"],
    ["N_d1", "N_d2", "R9"],
    ["N_d2", "N_d3", "R10"],
    ["N_d3", "B", "R11"]
  ]
}</final_answer>
